course_name_original: Methods and models for management engineering (146003)
course_name_en: Methods and models for management engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Identify the main quantitative problems related to various industrial and production processes.
Describe and model these problems from a mathematical perspective.
Solve them using the methods covered during the course.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to linear programming with examples and geometric interpretations
Study of the linear programming model and its mathematical properties
Analysis of minimum-cost network problems, minimum spanning tree, maximum flow, and shortest path problems
Integer and combinatorial optimization with practical applications
Markov chains: Chapman-Kolmogorov equation, classification of state types, long-term properties, and absorbing states
Decision-making problems based on Markov chains
Queueing Theory: Examples and basic structures, Little’s formula, properties of the exponential distribution
Analysis of single- and multi-server queues with exponential service times
Decisions on the optimal number of servers to use
Inventory Management: Determination of the optimal order quantity
Inventory theory under uncertainty, the “newsvendor problem,” and overbooking management
Introduction to simulation methods for analyzing complex systems
teaching_methods: Classroom exercises (modeling and solving problems, including with computers)
assessment_rules: The exam will consist of theoretical and practical questions and will require the ability to interpret and formulate the models studied in class.
bibliography: Hillier, F. S., & Lieberman, G. J.: Introduction to Operations Research. McGraw-Hill Science.
Hillier, F. S., & Lieberman, G. J. (2015). Introduction to operations research (10th ed.). McGraw-Hill Education.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Industriale (Industrial Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
